decisions.decision: Is DDPM sampling a good replacement for current GAN generation stack?
decisions.answer: partially: diffusion can match GAN image quality but sampling is much slower; suitability depends on whether your use case tolerates seconds-per-image latency.
decisions.notes: R1 (speed): For 256×256 CelebA-HQ/LSUN, sampling 128 images takes 300 s, about 2.3 s per image on TPU v3-8, i.e., full seconds not milliseconds [e22df3321d2941a1]. CIFAR-10 sampling is faster (256 images in 17 s, ~0.07 s per image) but still involves 1000 reverse steps [e22df3321d2941a1][3ee85dfaabd16f7f], much slower than one-shot GANs. R2 (stability): The paper describes a likelihood-based variational objective with Gaussian KLs [976fab954096b5d8][a6376ae2db7a6517] and modest hyperparameter search transferred across datasets [40de030796b3d32a], and notes that a reweighted objective improves sample quality [78f2a2312b837bff]. This supports more principled, stable training than typical GANs, but explicit comparisons on mode collapse are not provided. R3 (sharpness): The text references CelebA-HQ 256×256 interpolations and nearest neighbors [05e9701f321c9f11][5651007947ccee1d], implying visually plausible, detailed faces, but sharpness is not quantified; assessment is largely qualitative. R4 (parity with ProgressiveGAN): The provided chunks include the ProgressiveGAN citation [f1afe95e7b2ff529] but no explicit claim of sample-quality parity with ProgressiveGAN, so this is unknown. Overall, diffusion models achieve FID/IS comparable to strong GANs on CIFAR-10 [ecf16a1e8e178a04] and have principled training, but their multi-second sampling for 256×256 images makes them a poor drop-in replacement for latency-sensitive GAN stacks; they are better suited where quality and likelihood matter more than throughput.
